notes: Primary metric rmse_smoke_episodes is RMSE of the q50 forecast (ug/m3, +6 h) over rows where HMS shows medium/heavy smoke at the monitor at the target time (HMS is used only to select rows, never as input to scoring). LOWER is better.

CIs: day-block bootstrap over UTC issue days (per-day sufficient statistics, seed 0). Rows within a day across monitors are resampled together, so the CI reflects day-to-day and not monitor-level variability.
CSI/POD/FAR use obs and q50 > 35.4 ug/m3. Persistence beats the model on CSI/POD on val; the CNN wins RMSE/MAE. HMS adds nothing measurable on val (the no-HMS ablation is equal or better).
q90_coverage uses the raw q90 head; q90_coverage_shifted adds the val-fitted frozen log shift from models/smoke/calibration.json (the adapter does not apply it). Nothing is refit or tuned on test.
AQS hour value labelled t covers t..t+1 h, so the newest history hour is available at t+1 h: up to 1 h latency leak in the history features (spec-mandated). HRRR-Smoke store is 9 km (81 km patch).

Calibrated HRRR baseline uses the frozen train-fit models/smoke/massden_calibration.json; linear regression is fitted on a 400k-row TRAIN subsample (seed 0). Baseline rows with an all-NaN history (persistence) are dropped for that baseline only.

test_spatial = rows at the 198 spatially held-out monitors (inside the test year, never seen in train/val); the main model and baselines are scored on it as an extra split key. case_holdout is empty for smoke (no quarantined smoke days), so there is no case_holdout key.
